newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr rules roost against mark, stocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr rules roost against mark, stocks mixed.

text.p: The rampant dollar paused just below a six-year high against the weary mark on Friday, with some analysts saying the mark could sink further.

The continued strength of the U.S. currency, which made a brief sally above 1.84 marks, gave the German and French share markets further support, though Frankfurt ended a record-breaking week slightly down.
European bourses got a further boost when Wall Street opened firmer, despite the latest U.S. economic indicator to come in stronger than expected.
Currency dealers said the apparent tolerance of Germany's Bundesbank to the weak mark and the lack of support from the central bank's council meeting on Thursday had lifted the dollar.

The dollar was also up against the Swiss franc, climbing above 1.51 to reach its highest since August 1993. It was at 1.5150 at 1430 GMT. The Swiss franc's slide has dented its status as a safe haven in times of trouble, for example should the move to European and economic union unravel.

A press statement after Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting, its last before the four-week summer recess, said the central bank was paying attention to developments in the mark and financial markets.

"This was pretty bland so it was not hard to take dollar/mark higher," said a U.S. bank dealer. "But we've had more Buba comments since then which is giving people something to chew on into the weekend."

The dollar stood at 1.8350 marks at 1430 GMT after touching a fresh six-year high earlier of 1.8403. It was at 1.8315 late Thursday in Europe. Against the yen, it moved back towards its earlier, near one-month highs, and stood at 116.45 yen by midafternoon.
In Europe's share markets, London's FTSE 100 was showing a 10.0 point loss at 1430 GMT, when the index stood at 4,852.9, having touched a low of 4,834.8 earlier.
The market recovered a touch when Wall Street opened firmer and sprinted some 30 points higher in the first 30 minutes of trading, taking the U.S. blue-chip benchmark to around 8,145 points.
Wall Street latest romp higher came despite figures showing that U.S. durable goods orders for June were stronger than expected and injected interest-rate anxiety into the market again.
But strategists said bearish interpretations of the numbers were overridden by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's calming noises on the U.S. economy and inflation earlier this week.
"The market is biased to be bullish," Bernard Jensen, trader at Fuji Securities in New York, told Reuters TV, referring to U.S. Treasury bonds.
T-bonds turned higher after an initial fall after the data, which showed a rise of 2.3 percent for durable goods orders in June compared with an expected rise of 1.4 percent.
German shares closed a lacklustre floor session down nearly half a percent after trading sideways to cap a record-breaking week.

The DAX-30 index ended bourse dealing down 18.10 points at 4,317.64 -- about 90 points off Wednesday's all-time high of 4,406.09 -- as most shares failed to gain much impetus from the strong dollar and its brief foray over 1.84 marks.

But dealers said Friday's pause should not keep the DAX from continuing its upward charge until nearing resistance pegged at around 4,400 points. "For next week I expect the market to continue rising," one trader said.
French stocks were in bullish mood, and the CAC-40 index was up 50.37 points, or 1.7 percent, at 3,023.90 by 1430 GMT, having seesawed around the 3,000 level earlier.
The market was encouraged by the stronger dollar and Wall Street's overnight close at a record high, its third in a row. The U.S. market's strong opening added to the bullishness.
Rhone-Poulenc SA shares were up 3.5 percent at 257.2 francs after the chemicals group reported a 20.2 percent rise in second-quarter net income. Brokers said the results were excellent.
Peugeot Citroen rose an impressive 6.48 percent to 690 francs, helped by recent recommendations on the French car sector. Brokers said Peugeot is catching up with Renault's recent rally.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8350 marks and 116.45 yen compared with 1.8295 marks and 115.85 yen in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 10.0 points at 4,852.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended down 18.10 points at 4,317.64.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 17.05 points at 2,990.58.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $324.50 an ounce after closing in London at $322.65 on Thursday.
